name: Endeavor
industry: talent agency and sports-media holding company
desc: Holding company for talent and media agencies, representing artists across film, TV, music and publishing.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Silver Lake at USD 13bn; completed 24 March 2025
sponsorships: Represents the NFL and NHL; majority owner of TKO (WWE, UFC)
markets: Talent representation and media worldwide, with a Chinese subsidiary and holdings in UFC, WWE and EuroLeague ventures.
rationale: Owns UFC and WWE through TKO; F1 hospitality and content tie-ins fit its live-sports and entertainment portfolio.

name: Walgreens
desc: Runs Walgreens and Duane Reade retail pharmacies in the US; parent formerly also owned Boots.
capacity_detail: Walgreens Boots Alliance taken private by Sycamore Partners for USD 10bn; completed August 2025
markets: Walgreens stores in all 50 US states, Washington DC, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.
rationale: Mass-market US pharmacy brand could use F1's growing US audience, especially around the Miami, Austin and Las Vegas races.

name: Hologic
desc: Medical technology company focused on women's health, selling diagnostics, surgical and medical imaging devices.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Blackstone and TPG for USD 18.3bn including debt; completed 2026
sponsorships: Title sponsor of the WTA Tour and official health partner of the WTA (from 2022)
markets: Sells diagnostics and imaging worldwide, with operations in the US, UK, Spain, Finland and Germany.
rationale: Already invests in global sport through the WTA; F1 Academy and women-in-motorsport programmes match its women's-health positioning.

name: Nord Anglia Education
desc: International private school operator with over 80 day and boarding schools in 37 countries.
ownership: private equity: Neuberger Berman, EQT and CPP Investments consortium
capacity_detail: Acquired by consortium led by Neuberger Berman with EQT and CPP Investments for USD 14.5bn; completed March 2025
markets: More than 80 schools in 37 countries with over 100,000 students across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Americas.
rationale: Premium international schools target globally mobile affluent families, the same audience F1 reaches in Asia and the Middle East.

name: Dayforce
desc: Cloud human capital management platform covering payroll, tax, benefits, HR, workforce management and recruiting.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Thoma Bravo for about USD 12.3bn; completed 4 February 2026
markets: Payroll and HR software for employers in North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, Asia and Australia.
rationale: Enterprise HR software rivals such as Workday and UKG already use F1 for brand and B2B hospitality.

name: Adevinta
desc: Online classifieds group running marketplaces such as Leboncoin, Kleinanzeigen, Marktplaats, Subito and Kijiji.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Permira and Blackstone consortium for USD 13bn; closed May 2024
markets: Online classifieds brands including Leboncoin, Kleinanzeigen, Marktplaats, Subito and Kijiji across Europe and beyond.
rationale: Car and motoring classifieds such as Automobile.it reach motoring fans across F1's core European markets.

name: Squarespace
desc: Software-as-a-service company offering website building, hosting, domain registration, e-commerce and scheduling tools.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Permira for USD 7.2bn; completed October 2024
sponsorships: New York Knicks jersey patch (2017); Super Bowl advertising 2014-2026
markets: Serves small businesses, creators and online sellers worldwide; area served listed as worldwide.
rationale: Heavy brand advertiser (Super Bowl) seeking global reach; rival Wix-style web tools and Vercel already sponsor F1.

name: Nuvei
desc: Global payments technology company providing payment processing and acquiring for online and in-person transactions.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Advent International for about USD 6.3bn; completed 15 November 2024
markets: Payments in Canada, Latin America, Mexico, Colombia, Japan, Australia, Europe, Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Payments rivals Stripe, Visa, Mastercard and Cash App all use F1 to reach merchants and consumers globally.

name: Darktrace
desc: British cybersecurity company using unsupervised machine learning to detect and respond to threats in real time.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Thoma Bravo for USD 5.3bn; completed 1 October 2024
sponsorships: McLaren Racing partner (2020), extended to Arrow McLaren IndyCar team (2021)
markets: Offices in Cambridge, London, San Francisco, Singapore and The Hague, selling worldwide.
rationale: Has motorsport history with McLaren; cyber rivals CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Cato Networks are active F1 partners.

name: Instructure
desc: Educational technology company that develops Canvas, a web-based learning management system for schools and universities.
capacity_detail: Taken private by KKR and Dragoneer for USD 4.8bn; completed November 2024
markets: Canvas learning platform serves schools and universities worldwide.
rationale: F1 in Schools and STEM programmes give an education-software brand credible engagement with students and institutions.

name: Kahoot!
desc: Norwegian game-based learning platform where users create and play multiple-choice quizzes in browser or app.
ownership: private equity: Goldman Sachs Asset Management-led consortium
capacity_detail: Acquired by investor group including Goldman Sachs Asset Management for USD 1.72bn; delisted from Oslo in January 2024
markets: Platform available in 18 languages with billions of players worldwide.
rationale: Quiz-based fan engagement and STEM learning content could pair with F1's young global fan base.

name: Zuora
desc: Software for businesses to launch and manage subscription services, including recurring billing and revenue recognition.
ownership: private equity: Silver Lake and GIC
capacity_detail: Taken private by Silver Lake and GIC for USD 1.7bn; completed 14 February 2025
markets: Serves subscription businesses in North America, Europe, the UK, Australia and New Zealand.
rationale: Enterprise SaaS peers use F1 hospitality for B2B selling; subscription-economy story suits F1's media business.

name: Rover
desc: Online marketplace where people buy and sell pet care such as pet sitting, dog boarding and walking.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Blackstone for USD 2.3bn; completed February 2024
markets: Pet-care marketplace in the United States and Western Europe.
rationale: Consumer marketplace with US and European presence; F1 fan reach in both, though fit is modest.

name: Everbridge
desc: Enterprise software that sends alerts and shares information about critical events for safety and business continuity.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Thoma Bravo for about USD 1.8bn; closed July 2024
markets: Serves government and corporate clients worldwide, including the US, Norway, Peru and Australia.
rationale: Event-safety software has a natural showcase at large live events such as Grands Prix.

name: Olo
desc: Open SaaS platform helping restaurant brands grow orders, run operations and improve guest experience.
capacity_detail: Take-private by Thoma Bravo valued at about USD 2bn; completed (reported 15 September 2025)
markets: Serves over 800 restaurant brands across roughly 90,000 locations.
rationale: B2B restaurant tech with limited consumer brand; F1 hospitality could reach restaurant-brand executives.

name: Jeppesen
desc: Provides aeronautical charts, navigational information, flight planning products and operations software for aviation.
capacity_detail: Boeing Digital Aviation Solutions (Jeppesen, ForeFlight) sold to Thoma Bravo for USD 10.55bn; closed November 2025
markets: Offices in the US, Germany, Italy, UK, Sweden, Australia and Poland, serving airlines and pilots worldwide.
rationale: Newly independent aviation-tech brand needs its own identity; F1's engineering and logistics story fits its pilot audience.

name: OneStream
desc: Enterprise finance platform for the CFO office covering close, consolidation, reporting, planning and forecasting.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Hg for USD 6.4bn all-cash; completed 1 April 2026
markets: Sells finance software to enterprises; operations in the US.
rationale: Finance-software peers such as Workday, SAP and Oracle use F1 to court CFOs; Hg ownership supports European reach.

name: Jamf
desc: Software company making Jamf Pro, a device management system mainly for Apple macOS, iOS and iPadOS.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Francisco Partners for USD 2.2bn; completed 30 January 2026
markets: Device management software for organisations running Apple Mac, iPhone and iPad fleets.
rationale: IT-management rivals such as NinjaOne and ThreatLocker already sponsor F1 teams to reach IT buyers.

name: Fuji Soft
desc: Japanese systems developer and IT services company, formerly Tokyo-listed, with record revenue of JPY 317.5bn.
capacity_detail: KKR completed tender offer valuing the company at over USD 4bn; February 2025
markets: Systems development and IT services, chiefly in Japan.
rationale: Japanese IT services firm could use the Suzuka Grand Prix and Honda's F1 return to build profile.

name: AirTrunk
desc: Asia-Pacific data centre operator with more than 3 GW of operating and planned capacity across 20 sites.
ownership: private equity: Blackstone and CPP Investments
capacity_detail: Acquired by Blackstone and CPP Investments for AUD 24bn (USD 16bn); completed December 2024
markets: Data centres in Australia, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, Hong Kong and India.
rationale: Data-centre and AI infrastructure peers CoreWeave, VAST Data and Introl sponsor F1; Asia races match its footprint.

name: Network International
desc: Digital payments solutions company serving merchants and financial institutions across the Middle East and Africa.
capacity_detail: Brookfield-led consortium acquired 100% for GBP 2.2bn (USD 2.8bn); completed 17 September 2024
markets: Serves customers in 50 countries across the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Gulf payments leader; Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Saudi and Qatar Grands Prix give regional brand visibility.

name: Keywords Studios
desc: Provides art, engineering, testing, audio, translation, localisation and player support services to the video game industry.
ownership: private equity: EQT (with Temasek and CPP Investments)
capacity_detail: Taken private by EQT-led consortium for about GBP 2.2bn; completed 24 October 2024
markets: Studios in Ireland, Italy, Japan, Canada, the US, France, Germany, the Philippines, Brazil, Australia and China.
rationale: Works for F1 game publishers' industry; F1 esports and gaming tie-ins suit a B2B games-services brand.

name: Subway
desc: Fast-food franchise focused on submarine sandwiches and wraps, with over 37,000 locations in 100+ countries.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Roark Capital at a reported USD 9.6bn; completed 30 April 2024
sponsorships: NASCAR race title sponsorships (to 2016); Australia national football teams naming partner (from 2022)
markets: Over 37,000 locations in more than 102 countries and territories; about 61% in the United States.
rationale: Mass global consumer brand with motorsport history in NASCAR; rival McDonald's (Arcos Dorados) is already in F1.

name: Jersey Mike's
desc: American fast-casual submarine sandwich chain operating about 3,000 locations, mostly franchised.
capacity_detail: Blackstone bought a majority interest at USD 8bn valuation; completed January 2025
markets: About 3,000 sandwich shops, mainly in the United States.
rationale: Fast-growing US sandwich chain could ride F1's rising US audience, though its reach is essentially domestic.

name: Dave's Hot Chicken
desc: Fast-casual chain specialising in Nashville-style hot chicken, founded in Los Angeles in 2017.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Roark Capital in a deal valued at USD 1bn; June 2025
markets: Over 390 locations in the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and UAE.

signals.regions: Opened first Irish location in Dublin (Jun 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave%27s_Hot_Chicken)

rationale: Youth-oriented, international expansion into UK and Gulf matches F1's young fan base and Middle East races.

name: R1 RCM
desc: Revenue cycle management company serving hospitals, health systems and physician groups in the United States.
ownership: private equity: TowerBrook and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice
capacity_detail: Taken private by TowerBrook and CD&R valuing it at USD 8.9bn; completed November 2024
markets: Serves US hospitals, health systems and physician groups.
rationale: B2B US healthcare services firm; F1 fit is limited to corporate hospitality for hospital-system clients.

name: Patterson Companies
desc: Distributes dental and veterinary supplies through Patterson Dental, Patterson Veterinary and Animal Health International.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Patient Square Capital for USD 4.1bn; completed 17 April 2025
markets: Operates in the United States, Canada and the UK.
rationale: B2B dental and veterinary distributor with limited consumer brand; F1 relevance is low beyond hospitality.

name: Premier Inc.
desc: American healthcare company that started as a hospital buying group combining purchasing to lower costs.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Patient Square Capital for USD 2.6bn; completed 25 November 2025
markets: Group purchasing and analytics for hospitals and health systems in the United States.
rationale: US hospital purchasing group with little consumer or international angle for an F1 partnership.

name: Hillenbrand
desc: Global industrial company providing engineered processing equipment for durable plastics, food and recycling markets.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Lone Star at enterprise value of about USD 3.8bn; completed 10 February 2026
markets: Serves processing customers in plastics, food and recycling worldwide.
rationale: Engineering-led industrial brand; F1 B2B hospitality could support customer relationships, but consumer fit is weak.

name: Sealed Air
desc: Packaging company known for Cryovac food packaging and Bubble Wrap cushioning products, with 200+ locations globally.
capacity_detail: Taken private by CD&R at enterprise value of USD 10.3bn; closed 9 April 2026
markets: Global packaging operations with more than 200 locations.
rationale: Global B2B packaging brand; F1 sustainability and logistics stories offer a possible platform.

name: Triumph Group
desc: American supplier of aerospace services, structures, systems and support for aircraft makers and airlines.
ownership: private equity: Warburg Pincus and Berkshire Partners
capacity_detail: Taken private by Warburg Pincus and Berkshire Partners for about USD 3bn; completed July 2025
markets: Supplies aircraft manufacturers and airlines with structures, systems and support services.
rationale: Aerospace engineering supplier; an F1 technical partnership would support engineering recruitment and B2B profile.

name: Toshiba
desc: Japanese multinational making power and infrastructure systems, elevators, semiconductors, hard drives, batteries and IT solutions.
ownership: private equity: Japan Industrial Partners consortium
capacity_detail: Taken private by JIP-led consortium for JPY 2tn (about USD 15bn); completion announced 22 December 2023
markets: Worldwide, with subsidiaries in the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Australia, China, Europe and the Gulf.
rationale: Global electronics brand rebuilding after delisting; Japanese peers Honda and Toyota anchor F1 and the Suzuka race.

name: Hargreaves Lansdown
desc: The UK's largest retail investment platform, offering ISAs, pensions, savings, annuities and income drawdown.
ownership: private equity: CVC, Nordic Capital and ADIA
capacity_detail: Taken private by CVC, Nordic Capital and ADIA valuing it at GBP 5.4bn; scheme sanctioned March 2025
markets: Serves retail investors and savers across the United Kingdom through its investment platform.
rationale: UK investing brand targeting affluent savers; Silverstone and F1's UK fan base fit, as eToro and Public sponsor teams.

name: Dechra
desc: Develops and markets veterinary pharmaceuticals for companion and farm animals in Europe and the United States.
capacity_detail: Taken private by EQT valuing it at GBP 4.5bn; completed 16 January 2024
markets: Two divisions: European Pharmaceuticals and U.S. Pharmaceuticals, selling veterinary medicines.
rationale: Animal-health pharma serving vets, a professional audience; F1 relevance is limited beyond corporate hospitality.

name: Spectris
desc: British supplier of precision instrumentation and controls used in research and industrial measurement.
capacity_detail: Acquired by KKR at GBP 4.7bn (USD 6.46bn) including debt; completed December 2025
markets: Precision instruments sold to industrial and research customers.
rationale: Precision measurement is core to F1 engineering; a technical-partner role suits its customer base.

name: Dun & Bradstreet
desc: Provides commercial data, analytics and insights on 500 million business records for risk, supply and sales teams.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Clearlake in a deal valued at USD 7.7bn including debt; completed 26 August 2025
markets: Americas plus Europe, UK, Ireland, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and India.
rationale: Data and analytics brand; F1's data storytelling suits B2B rivals already partnering with teams.

name: Envestnet
desc: Develops and distributes wealth management software and products for financial advisors and institutions.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Bain Capital-led group valued at USD 4.5bn; completion announced 25 November 2024
markets: Serves financial advisors and wealth-management institutions in the United States.
rationale: Wealth-tech serving advisers; F1 hospitality courts high-net-worth clients, as Edward Jones and Nuveen do.

name: SolarWinds
desc: Develops software helping businesses monitor and manage networks, systems and IT infrastructure.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Turn/River for USD 4.4bn; closed 18 April 2025
markets: Sells IT monitoring and management software to businesses worldwide.
rationale: IT-operations rivals Dynatrace, Splunk and NinjaOne are F1 partners; Austin home race at COTA.

name: Barnes Group
desc: Global industrial technology and aerospace manufacturer and service provider based in Connecticut.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Apollo funds for USD 3.6bn; completed January 2025
markets: Industrial and aerospace manufacturing operations serving global customers.
rationale: Engineering manufacturer; an F1 technical partnership is possible, but consumer brand fit is weak.

name: Skechers
desc: American multinational making lifestyle and performance footwear, clothing and accessories for adults and children.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 8.97bn in 2024; taken private by 3G Capital, completed September 2025
sponsorships: Kit sponsor of Mohun Bagan Super Giant (from 2024); W Racing Team sports-car partner; Super Bowl advertiser
markets: Sells worldwide through own stores and retailers, including European distribution from Liege, Belgium.
rationale: Already backs W Racing Team in sports-car racing; Puma and New Era show footwear and apparel brands thrive in F1.

name: Clear Channel Outdoor
desc: Multinational outdoor advertising company running billboards, transit and airport displays.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Mubadala at enterprise value of USD 6.2bn; completed 2026
markets: Billboards in 43 of the top 50 US markets, plus Europe, Singapore, Latin America and Caribbean airports.
rationale: Media owner could trade inventory for race-city visibility; Abu Dhabi owner Mubadala is close to F1's Gulf calendar.

name: Select Medical
desc: Owns long-term acute care and inpatient rehabilitation hospitals plus occupational health and physical therapy clinics.
ownership: private equity: Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe and management
capacity_detail: Taken private by WCAS and management for USD 3.9bn; completed 2026
markets: Hospitals and outpatient clinics in the United States.
rationale: US physical-therapy brand; sports medicine angle exists but F1 fit is limited.

name: Senior plc
industry: engineered components for aerospace and vehicles
desc: Holding company for manufacturing firms making components and systems for vehicle, aerospace and energy customers.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Tinicum and Blackstone for USD 1.9bn; acquired October 2026
markets: Global group of engineering businesses serving aerospace, vehicle and energy markets.
rationale: UK engineering supplier near F1's Motorsport Valley; a technical partnership would support engineering recruitment.

name: Nippon Sheet Glass
desc: Glass maker that owns Pilkington, supplying architectural and automotive glass worldwide.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Apollo funds for USD 3.7bn; delisting from Tokyo Stock Exchange September 2026
markets: Sales about 40% Europe, 25% Asia including Japan, and 35% North and South America.
rationale: Automotive glass supplier with Pilkington brand; F1 technical link to car makers is credible.

name: Qube Holdings
desc: Diversified Australian logistics company running rail freight, stevedoring at 29 ports and warehousing.
ownership: private equity: Macquarie Asset Management-led consortium
capacity_detail: Taken private by Macquarie Asset Management-led consortium for USD 8.3bn; delisted July 2026
markets: Rail freight, stevedoring at 29 ports and warehousing across Australia.
rationale: Australian logistics leader; Melbourne Grand Prix offers domestic visibility, though reach is limited.

name: Boralex
desc: Develops, builds and operates wind, hydroelectric, solar and storage renewable energy facilities.
ownership: private equity: Brookfield and La Caisse
capacity_detail: Taken private by Brookfield and La Caisse for USD 6.5bn; completed 2026
markets: Renewable plants in Canada, France, the United Kingdom and the United States.
rationale: Renewables producer could align with F1's net-zero 2030 and the Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal.

name: Avanos Medical
desc: Medical technology company making digestive health, respiratory, pain management and intravenous therapy devices.
capacity_detail: Taken private by AIP for about USD 1.272bn; completed July 2026
markets: Sells digestive, respiratory, pain management and IV therapy devices to hospitals.
rationale: Hospital medical device maker with clinical buyers; F1 relevance is low beyond corporate hospitality.

name: NextGen Healthcare
desc: Develops electronic health record and practice management software for medical and dental practices.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Thoma Bravo at enterprise value of USD 1.8bn; completed November 2023
markets: Serves medical and dental practices in the United States with EHR software.
rationale: US health-IT vendor selling to practices; F1 fit is limited to B2B hospitality and recruitment.

name: PowerSchool
desc: Cloud-based K-12 education software vendor used by schools for student information and learning.
capacity_detail: Taken private by Bain Capital for USD 5.6bn; completed 1 October 2024
markets: Serves K-12 schools and districts with cloud education software.
rationale: Education software vendor; F1 in Schools STEM programmes offer only a niche brand fit.
